rights_note: The Met's Open Access images of public-domain works are released CC0. Used only as a reference for the kinds of trimming, cloth and hats the 1904 women's dress is drawn with (T-3553); nothing is traced or sampled from it.
access_notes: Viewed 2026-11-14 (T-3553) from the museum's open-access image and object record: a straw tricorne hat: its brim turned up and waved, trimmed with white and black ostrich plumes and a dotted silk ribbon. A real garment, American, not of Chicago and not of anyone drawn in the town.
note: One of the T-3553 finery references (docs/RESEARCH/finery-3553/README.md): the trimmed picture hat.
what_it_supplies: a wide trimmed straw hat of the years, with curled ostrich plumes and ribbon
what_it_does_not_supply: how any Prairie Avenue woman dressed, or the colour of any dress she owned
how often such a dress was worn on a Chicago street in 1904
